title: German AI Chip Startup Sparxity Closes Series A, Total Funding Reaches $90 Million
excerpt: The Dresden company formerly known as SpiNNcloud builds chips that skip unnecessary calculations in AI models. Lockheed Martin Ventures and GlobalFoundries joined the round, whose own size was not disclosed.
body:
• Sparxity, the Dresden-based AI chip company formerly known as SpiNNcloud, has closed a Series A round that brings its total funding to $90 million; the size of the Series A itself was not disclosed.
  • The round was led by ICM HPQC Fund, with Lockheed Martin Ventures, GlobalFoundries, GS Futures, Cloudberry Ventures, TGFS and the European Innovation Council Fund participating.
  • Sparxity builds chips around sparse computing — skipping calculations a model does not need — and is targeting up to 44 times faster inference on ultra-sparse models with its next-generation chip, a company target.
  • The company says it has completed three chip tapeouts, produced more than 70,000 chips, deployed 12 racks and signed more than 30 customers, and that revenue quadrupled between 2024 and 2025.

Sparxity, a German semiconductor and AI infrastructure company based in Dresden, has closed its Series A financing, bringing its cumulative funding to $90 million, the company announced. The money will support specialised chips designed to make AI inference more efficient by concentrating computing resources on the operations that are actually needed, according to Pulse 2.0. The company did not disclose how much new capital the Series A itself raised, so the $90 million figure is a cumulative total rather than fresh money.

Who Backed the Round

The round was led by ICM HPQC Fund, with participation from Lockheed Martin Ventures, GlobalFoundries, GS Futures, Cloudberry Ventures, TGFS and the European Innovation Council Fund, according to the company's Business Wire announcement. Individual investors included Richard Socher of Recursive Superintelligence and Nancy Xu, whose previous company Moonhub was acquired by Salesforce, alongside continued support from Atlantic and Silicon Catalyst.

Compute Only What Matters

Sparxity, formerly known as SpiNNcloud, builds full-stack computing systems around sparse processing. Most AI models activate only a small subset of their parameters for any given input; hardware built for that pattern can skip the remaining calculations instead of spending energy on them. The company's next-generation chip is being designed for fine-grained dynamic sparsity in AI inference, targeting performance improvements of up to 44 times faster inference for certain ultra-sparse models — a target the company sets for a chip still in development, as GamesBeat reported. Its SpiNNaker2 chip builds on the work of Steve Furber, who co-designed the original ARM processor.

The company says it has completed three semiconductor tapeouts, manufactured more than 70,000 chips and deployed 12 racks, and that revenue quadrupled between 2024 and 2025 with continued momentum in 2026.

Deployments at Jülich and Deutsche Telekom

The funding follows two commercial steps. Sparxity announced a multimillion-dollar deployment of its systems at the Jülich Supercomputing Centre in Germany, part of Forschungszentrum Jülich and home to Europe's first exascale supercomputer. It also established a partnership with Deutsche Telekom to integrate its sparse-native technology into the data centre infrastructure of its T-Systems subsidiary, with a first deployment due in 2028 under a letter of intent, according to Data Center Dynamics.

Founded in 2021, Sparxity positions its systems as a complement to GPU hardware rather than a replacement: the bet is that model builders keep adopting sparser architectures faster than general-purpose chips adapt. Whether that holds depends on the next-generation chip now being funded — and on the 30-plus customers the company says it has signed across the United States and Europe converting early deployments into volume orders.
